speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I notice you have yellowish coloring of your skin and eyes, which suggests jaundice. To help determine the cause, have you experienced any abdominal pain, nausea, or fever recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and recent agitation, have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools, and are you experiencing any right upper quadrant abdominal pain? I also need to ask if you have had any recent fevers or chills.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your risk factors, I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis, so I will order immediate liver function tests and viral serologies. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Hepatitis_A_IgM, Hepatitis_B_Surface_Antigen, Hepatitis_C_Antibody

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Panel: Bilirubin 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity < 40% (reduced), INR 1.5 (elevated); Hepatitis_A_IgM: NORMAL READINGS; Hepatitis_B_Surface_Antigen: NORMAL READINGS; Hepatitis_C_Antibody: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative viral hepatitis tests and coagulopathy suggest acute liver failure, possibly from drug toxicity or another etiology. Do you recall ingesting any over-the-counter medications, particularly acetaminophen, or any herbal supplements recently? REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen_Level, Autoimmune_Hepatitis_Panel, Ceruloplasmin

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetaminophen_Level: 15 μg/mL (therapeutic range); Autoimmune_Hepatitis_Panel: Anti-smooth muscle antibody negative, Anti-mitochondrial antibody negative, ANA negative; Ceruloplasmin: 18 mg/dL (low)

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the low ceruloplasmin levels and your age, I suspect Wilson's disease, so I need to assess for neurological signs. Have you experienced any tremors, difficulty speaking, or changes in your handwriting recently? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: The low ceruloplasmin and acute liver failure in a young adult strongly point to Wilson's disease, but I need to confirm hepatic copper accumulation. REQUEST TEST: 24_Hour_Urine_Copper, Serum_Copper

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of low ceruloplasmin, low serum copper, and elevated urine copper in a young patient with acute liver failure is diagnostic for Wilson's disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Wilson's Disease
